note: The teacher's requirements and where the project meets them. Written by hand from the five course guides, the teacher's notes and the audit of 2026-11-18 (docs/test-report.md); keep it in step with the report.

items.requirement: Design a data-warehouse star schema for a flight journey; the fact is the flight segment fact table.
items.evidence: Star schema with one fact table (Fact_FlightSegment) and eight dimension tables; report section 3.2.

items.requirement: Preprocess the data set and create stopover information from the transit airports; stopover landing and take-off times are not modelled.
items.evidence: 95 of 600 segments carry a transit airport; no stopover time is stored; report section 3.1.

items.requirement: Show the preprocessed schema and some data instances in the report.
items.evidence: Report section 3.1: the rules table before and after, and nine rows of the fact table with all 15 columns.

items.requirement: Fact-table rules: at least 20 departure and 20 landing airports, 20 stopover rows, 50 passengers, 6 months, 10 airlines; PlaneID and CabinID neither blank nor constant.
items.evidence: All 17 automatic checks pass after preprocessing (9 of 17 before).

items.requirement: Schema advice: date-only time dimension, airport separate from city, flight times on the flight, stopover airport on the fact.
items.evidence: DimDate holds days only; DimAirport is its own dimension; departure and arrival times sit on DimTicket; TransitAirportKey is on the fact.

items.requirement: Build the data warehouse in SQL Server; the creation statements take no more than one third of the report.
items.evidence: FlightDW in SQL Server 2022, cube in Analysis Services; the creation statements (Appendix A) take 3 of 29 pages.

items.requirement: Seven or more OLAP operations (drill down, roll up, slice, dice, rank, moving average, top N), three MDX statements each.
items.evidence: Eight operations with three statements each (running total added), plus four stopover statements: 28 MDX statements, all checked against T-SQL answer keys.

items.requirement: Analyse the stopovers of the flights.
items.evidence: Four stopover statements: top hubs, price with and without stopover, stopover share per airline, stopover-only routes.

items.requirement: A report with meaningful queries, examples and running-result screenshots.
items.evidence: Report section 3.3: every one of the 28 statements has its question, its SSMS screenshot and an analysis; one full worked example per operation.

items.requirement: Report format: cover with all members, group, teacher and date; Times New Roman 11; captions (figures below, tables above, numbered separately); page numbers; one named part per member in sections 4 and 5; SWJTU references.
items.evidence: Built by tools/build_report.py with these rules and checked by tests.

items.requirement: The software environment (versions, installation, settings) in at most one A4 page.
items.evidence: Section 3.2, 'Software environment and configuration': about half a page.

items.requirement: About 25 pages; one MDX example within half a page; MDX, not SQL, for OLAP; no large blank space in images; complete MDX statements may go to an appendix.
items.evidence: 29 pages (the team's agreed limit); each worked example measured at 36 to 49 % of a page; all OLAP in MDX; screenshots cropped; all 28 statements in full in Appendix B.
